Authentic second-issue Academy holdings: 3 of 40 parale on azure and 19 on white; 2 of 80 on azure and 9 on white; 2 of the 5-parale newspaper value.

provenance: deaccessioned by the Romanian Academy to dealer Onig Tulbendjan
value: exchanged for 13 stamps worth 2,065 French francs
note: On 2 October 1939 the Academy traded a 'used and damaged' 54-parale Cap de Bour to dealer Onig Tulbendjan for 13 stamps worth 2,065 French francs (Yvert 1939).

provenance: Al. G. Cantacuzino collection (donated to the Society of Public Servants)
note: The Cantacuzino collection held, first issue: 2 of 27 parale, 2 of 54, 1 of 108; second issue: 6 of 5 parale, 18 of 40, 16 of 80.

provenance: given by Alexandru Cantacuzino to Queen Elisabeta
note: In 1894, for the royal silver wedding, Alexandru Cantacuzino gave Queen Elisabeta a Cap de Bour stamp (press dubbed it a 'Moldavian bear's-head' stamp).

marking: old letters franked with Cap de Bour
provenance: found in the attic of the Palace of Public Servants, discovered by Ion Papae
note: During WWII a large cache of old letters, many franked with Cap de Bour, was found in the attic of the Palace of Public Servants (Piata Victoriei) by Ion Papae, then stolen during an air raid.

marking: near-complete Romanian collection 'starting with Cap de Bou'
note: The Saint-Georges Museum in Bârlad held a nearly complete Romanian collection 'beginning with the Cap de Bou' (the author doubts an accompanying claim of sheets in 480/600/840-lei values).

marking: described as the museum's rarest stamp
note: In a 1939 article Emilian Costescu singled out the Saint-Georges Museum's rarest stamp: 'the beautiful 80-parale Cap de Bou'.

marking: original printing dies/matrices and approved essay sheets
provenance: Stamp Factory / State Bank Printing House (later Poșta); visited 1 June 1945
note: The Stamp Factory held the original dies used to print both 1858 Cap de Bour issues and their essays (often full sheets with printing-approval signatures); philatelists viewed them 1 June 1945.
Constantin N. Minescu recorded that in 1906 the original cliches used to print the Cap de Bour stamps were held at the 'National Museum'.

provenance: Prahova County Museum of History and Archaeology
note: The Prahova County Museum displays one first-issue Cap de Bour stamp; the 'Lucian Blaga' Central University Library in Cluj-Napoca also holds a first-issue example.

marking: 4 first-issue stamps + many second-issue singles and blocks
note: At the Timișoara exhibition, Matheescu-Sinaia showed two collections with 4 first-issue Cap de Bour and many second-issue singles and blocks, estimated (dubiously) at 10 million lei.

marking: over 25 first-issue and over 250 second-issue on display
note: The 1924 Bucharest exhibition presented over 25 first-issue Cap de Bour stamps and over 250 second-issue examples to the public.

marking: 'Zimbrul si Vulturul' newspaper franked with 8 stamps; original dies also shown
provenance: exhibited by Muzeul National Filatelic at EFIRO 2008
note: At EFIRO 2008 the National Philatelic Museum displayed the original Cap de Bour printing dies and the 'Zimbrul si Vulturul' newspaper franked with eight 5-parale second-issue stamps.
Directorate report records exactly 24,064 first-issue stamps printed in two batches (11 and 21 July 1858), per value 6016×27, 10016×54, 2016×81, 6016×108 parale.
First order split 'for Directorate and for outside': 10,000 stamps; 6,000 (3,000+3,000); 1,000 of the 108-parale value for registered letters; a note adds 1,000 more at 27 parale.
Stamp-workshop secretary's report No.62 accounts for 5,984 first-issue stamps in 187 sheets: 992×27, 992×54, 480×81, 3520×108 parale.
W-G cites a sheet of first-issue essais (54, 81, 108 machine-printed, 27 hand-struck) published by Minescu/Vișoianu in 'Die Postmarke' No.334, evidence of the printing method.
Directorate note distinguishes the 108-parale 'Cap de bou' cut round versus cut square ('taiat rotund' / 'taiat cvadratu'), a small official run.
Distribution list of 18,080 first-issue stamps of assorted values (per-value cells 9024, 5024, 2496, 1536 etc.), part of the 24,064 total handled by cashier N. Costin.
Focșani sameș's LISTA reconciles the four first-issue values (27/54/81/108): received from Directorate in August, used, remaining 1 Sept, and sent to outside expeditors (cells OCR-garbled).
Tecuci bureau return accounts for 75 stamps of 27 parale and 24 stamps of 108 parale, among the first-issue values handled that month.
Neamț-district return covers 338 stamps worth 448 lei (per-value cells incl. 184 and 18 stamps), first-issue accounting sent to the Directorate.
At dissolution of the first issue an appreciable number of 27-parale stamps was found at the Iași cashier from remainders collected from all Moldavian offices, amid a chronic 27-parale shortage.
W-G judges the existence of halves (bisects) of the 54-parale stamp not excluded, used because of the shortage of the 27-parale value.
Galați bureau reports 2,419 stamps sold 1 Sept–1 Oct 1858 (money paid to treasury), noting the first issue (27/54/81/108) circulated only 2 months.
12,308 first-issue stamps remained unsold and were annulled/destroyed (per-value remainder cells 2325, 5244, 3432, 1307; e.g. 7×81 and 2×108 parale in one tally).
W-G possesses in his own collection letters bearing the Târgu Frumos 1859 postmark, vindicating a bureau/postmark earlier contested as forged by Minescu and Racoviceanu.
The old small 1852 Fălticeni office stamp is found on letters and on stamps with dates 1/1, 2/2 … 12/12, confirming its authentic use before the round datestamps of 1858.
Ministry orders 20,000 second-issue stamps to be ready for 1 November 1858, including 3,000 of the 5-parale value for simple letters and registered items.
First second-issue printing of 10,816 stamps: 960×5, 7040×40 (1 leu), 2816×80 parale (2 lei), printed at the Atelia Timbrului.
A further batch of 9,216 second-issue stamps (4960×40, 2208×80, 2048×5 parale) brings the running total with the first 10,816 to 20,032 stamps.
Additional printing of 4,000 stamps of the 5-parale value (for gazettes), reported delivered to the Directorate 24 November 1858.
Ismail bureau consumed 61 stamps of 40 parale and 80 stamps of 80 parale in six weeks; 225 stamps had been sent to it under office No.2747 — early second-issue usage figures.
Galați end-of-December account finds unsold on hand 236 stamps at 2 lei (80 parale), 193 at 1 leu (40 parale) and a count at 5 parale, carried forward.
A unique example found on the face of a letter with an arrival cancel: an 80-parale stamp cut and used for a rare franking, W-G promising to publish it later.
Halves of the 80-parale stamp were found used in place of the 40-parale value, surviving in 2–3 examples, an extremely rare bisected franking.
An illustrated cover sent from Iași to Galați, registered and express, franked with 2 stamps of 80 parale.
An illustrated 1861 cover travelling from Wallachia into Moldova bearing the handstamps of both posts at Focșani, the interchange point after the 1859 union.
Reprint of 9,024 second-issue stamps (6016×40 / 1 leu and 3008×80 / 2 lei), 9,000 printed in 16 days as the workshop was also busy with the Timbru Domnesc sheets.
The Directorate queries why the small market town of Fălticeni needed a large supply — including 150 stamps of the 80-parale value — attributed to its annual fair traffic.
Order for 7,000 second-issue stamps: 5,000×40 (1 leu) and 2,000×80 (2 lei) parale.
W-G is convinced the majority of 40- and 80-parale stamps used at Fălticeni bear datestamps from the twenty fair days around 20 July 1859.

marking: framed FRANCO (Galatz No.2, Jassy, Leova, Darabani, Roman, Ismailu, Cahul, Botoșani, Tecuci, Neamțu, Ocna, Huși, Bacău, Focșani, Michaileni)
note: Plate reproduces the framed FRANCO handstamps introduced autumn 1859, illustrated struck on 40- and 80-parale second-issue stamps for many bureaus.
A Focșani/Ismail contra-adeverință notes a sheet (fila) of 40-parale = 32 lei and a sheet of 80-parale = 64 lei; Ismail's 200 lei could not buy complete sheets.
Order No.10529 printed 20,032 second-issue stamps: 12,000×40 (1 leu), 6016×80 (2 lei) and 2016×5 parale.
Reprint of 20,000 second-issue stamps: 12,000×40 (1 leu) and 8,000×80 (2 lei) parale.
Order for 40,000 second-issue stamps — 25,000×40 (1 leu) and 15,000×80 (2 lei) parale — the Directorate noting 20,000 stamps used in just 2 months.
25,000 stamps of 40 parale (exhausted after ~10.5 months by 31 March 1861) and 15,000 of 80 parale printed 3 June 1860 (exhausted after ~10 months), at ~2,000×40 and ~1,200×80 per month.
Second-issue stock figures 12,000×40 and 5,024×80 parale with monthly consumption ~2,000×40 and ~1,200×80, the values circulating from 1 November 1858 to June 1862.
W-G possesses the Iași bureau's stamp-consumption return for March 1860, Iași having the largest consumption (chiefly 5-parale stamps for franking gazettes).
Monthly sales for January and February 1861: 40 parale 990 and 749; 80 parale 611 and 520; 5 parale 255 and 158 stamps (totals 1,562 / 1,555).
Master table of second-issue 'Cap de Bou' stamps printed and circulated by value/date — 5, 40 and 80 parale columns (960/7040/2816, 2048/4960/2208, 2016/6016/3008, 4000/…), a six-figure total.
An illustrated cover of 1861 franked with a single 80-parale stamp on azure paper, cited as proof both azure and white papers were used to the last.
W-G cites the existence of letters dated 1858 franked with stamps on white paper (versus later azure) as documentary evidence of the two paper varieties.
Illustrated large 80-parale stamp on azure paper with the outer circle struck low, cancelled Jassy-Moldova, dated November 1861 (bottom frame broken).
Illustrated 5-parale stamp on white paper with left frame deformed, cancelled with the Roman-Moldova datestamp (outer circle fully broken).
The last 4,000 5-parale stamps had a cracked bottom frame; genuinely postmarked (e.g. at Bacău 1862) W-G calls this the rarest of all 'Cap de Bou' stamps of both issues.
Illustrated 5-parale stamp used in 1861 at the Iași office with the frame intact, paired against the later broken-frame variety.
A very interesting and rare piece: an 80-parale stamp serving as a 40-parale porto, sent from Roman on 4 June 1862, a late usage after the 1 May 1862 withdrawal order.

Table of second-issue (5/40/80) remainder stamps returned to the Directorate in 1862 by office: Michaileni 292, Botoșani 573, Bacău 776, Fălticeni 404, Bârlad 519, Huși 532, Focșani 215/478, Cahul 22.
Responding to a collector's request, the Director General of Posts sent 4 stamps each of the 5, 40 and 80 parale second-issue values (in their colours), documenting an official supply of specimens.
A letter from the foreigner Jakob Urbl attests that the 27-parale 'Cap de Bou' of the first issue was still not known abroad in 1864.
Order to print 4,000 stamps of the 5-parale gazette value; a proposed 10-parale gazette stamp was never issued, the 5-parale being introduced from 1 November 1858.
